solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Muscle — error mostly involving recall of another muscle

indicators.note: the shortened error wraps around the next piece, taking it into itself
most of the word is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the muscle's letters run backwards

parts.note: a pec is the short form of pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: An anatomy student's slip: confusing one muscle with another.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is British slang for a blunder; 'mostly' drops its last letter, and 'recall of' reads the chest muscle backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-headed upper-arm flexor is a standard example of a muscle.

clue.text: Live, being host to a pulse? A habit of the clean-living

indicators.note: the living word plays host, holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a throb is a pulse or beat

explanation.surface: Living with a heartbeat, a clean-living sort has an ascetic habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clean-living' puns on bathing: a bathrobe is the garb of those fresh from a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment, and a robe worn after bathing suits those who keep clean.

clue.text: Improve knowledge of belief system that is to limit tax

parts.note: a cult is a system of religious belief

indicators.note: the two letters bound the tax on either side

parts.note: IE is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Learning about a sect that seeks to cap taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cultivate an interest or skill is to develop and refine it.

clue.text: Vote to limit Scottish town staff list

indicators.note: the vote's letters enclose the town, limiting it

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A ballot to cap the number of workers in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: The payroll is the list of employees a company pays.

clue.text: Dance hall's success involving everybody beginning to rumba

indicators.note: the success word takes the following pieces into its middle

parts.note: a boom is a period of great success or prosperity
all means everybody

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the dance name is wanted

explanation.surface: A dance venue is thriving now that everyone has started doing the rumba.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'hall' is read as 'has', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom is a large room or venue built for dancing.

clue.text: A follower's strained, having accommodated day in hostile situation

indicators.note: the follower's letters take in the day letter

parts.note: a tagger is one who tags along, a follower; the 's adds S
drawn means strained or haggard

explanation.surface: A tag-along is tense after putting someone up for a day.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes just after the T of TAGGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at daggers drawn means being in bitter open hostility.

clue.text: Late arriving? Force girl to stay up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: drag is a resisting force in aerodynamics
gal is a dialect word for a girl

explanation.surface: Is someone arriving late because they pressured a girl into staying up?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjectival phrase and laggard can be an adjective, meaning slow or late.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a straggler, someone who falls behind and turns up late.

clue.text: New Zealand area identified in religious texts from the past

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
ago means in time gone by

explanation.surface: A New Zealand region named in ancient scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region in the south of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Responsible male character not providing name

indicators.note: the character word goes without the name letter

parts.note: nature means character or temperament

explanation.surface: A sensible man whose character is never named.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature person is adult and sensible, capable of taking responsibility.

clue.text: Tingling feeling in leg, smooth, and mostly uncalled-for

parts.note: pin is slang for a leg
to sand is to smooth

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: needless means unnecessary or uncalled-for

explanation.surface: A tingle in the leg, smoothed away, and mostly unwarranted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts NEEDLESS to NEEDLES; the 'and' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickling felt as a numb limb recovers is the idiom for that tingling sensation.

clue.text: End in victory after high score

indicators.note: the victory letter is sent after the word for high

parts.note: tall means high

indicators.note: the end of the word victory supplies one letter

explanation.surface: A team finally wins after racking up a big score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the end letter behind the word for high.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally is a running count or score, as in a points total.

clue.text: Bar covering archaeological work has soldier annoyed

indicators.note: the bar's letters go round the dig, covering it

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar
a dig is an archaeological excavation
a soldier ant is a worker caste ant, so ant is the crossword soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is cross because a pub has been built over an excavation site.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means angered by something felt to be unfair.

clue.text: Sport in America includes nothing drastic

indicators.note: the run of letters takes a further letter into itself

parts.note: RU is rugby union
US is the United States
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Some American sport involves no holding back at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is rugby union, abbreviated, not a verb; the O lands before the America letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous is disastrous or extreme in its effects, close to drastic.

clue.text: Mystical effect, showing happiness and sorrow both reduced

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: glad means showing happiness
to mourn is to show sorrow

explanation.surface: A spell that brings joy and sadness together, each in a lesser form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both reduced' cuts GLAD to GLA and MOURN to MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: In its old Scots sense, glamour was a magic spell or enchantment.

clue.text: Main issue: alarm about a couple of lands warring about English

indicators.note: the alarm word goes round everything that follows

parts.note: a bell rings as an alarm

indicators.note: the jumbled lands are wrapped around the next letter
lands at war are in turmoil, so the letters are jumbled
two copies of the word are taken

parts.note: land, singular, taken twice for a couple of lands

explanation.surface: The chief worry: a warning about two countries fighting over England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warring' scrambles LANDLAND to LLANDNDA, which 'about' wraps round E for LLANDENDA; A goes in front and BELL goes round all.
explanation.definitionFit: The be-all and end-all is the thing of supreme importance, the main issue.

clue.text: One who takes clarinets to play

indicators.note: the letters are played with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief who steals clarinets so he can play them.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits larceny, theft, so is a person who takes what is not theirs.

clue.text: Cordial brewed in estate

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture, so these letters are stirred together

explanation.surface: A cordial drink made on a country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed liqueur, and cordial is an old word for a liqueur.

clue.text: Don't lose rag (or rug)

parts.note: losing one's rag is British slang for losing one's temper; a rug is slang for a wig, so the idiom also reads as keeping a toupee in place

explanation.surface: Stay calm, and keep your toupee on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose your rag' is British for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom urges someone to stay calm, and literally means not losing a wig or hair.

clue.text: Show left some sunshine

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a ray is a single beam of sunlight

explanation.surface: A glimpse of sunshine appears on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent, to show.

clue.text: Boxing edge — Clay possibly displays transformative power

indicators.note: the rearranged letters box in the edge word, holding it inside
possibly signals the letters could be some other arrangement

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: Cassius Clay, with the edge in a boxing bout, shows his magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clay' tempts as Cassius Clay the boxer; 'possibly' scrambles it to ALCY, which goes round HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the supposed art of turning base metals into gold, hence any power to transform.

clue.text: Descriptive of stone tablets or collections of stones

definitions.meaning: relating to Moses, who received the stone tablets of the law
pictures made from small pieces of stone set together; the clue's plural stands for the art form

explanation.surface: A geologist describing tablets and assortments of rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: With a capital the word means 'of Moses', whose commandments came on stone tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalised sense relates to Moses; the common sense names inlaid patterns of small stones.

clue.text: Take notes days before bad smell returns around river

indicators.note: the turned letters go round the river letter
the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eves are the days before festivals or events
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Someone notes down a story of days before a stink comes back near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' makes EVESBO into OBSEVE, which 'around' wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch and remark on, as one does in taking notes.

clue.text: Started a fight

definitions.meaning: began working at something vigorously, past tense

explanation.definitionFit: Two words written apart mean began energetically; hyphenated, the phrase is a noun for a scrap.

clue.text: NASA's concern: alien interfering in moon samples?

indicators.note: the alien gets into the middle of the samples

parts.note: rocks brought back by astronauts are moon samples, the question mark flagging the example
ET is the film alien, extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: NASA worries an extraterrestrial has tampered with lunar rock samples.
explanation.definitionFit: Launch vehicles are a central concern of the American space agency.

clue.text: Back down about amount of energy in fading light

indicators.note: the energy unit sits in the middle of the two joined words

parts.note: aft means at the back of a ship
low means down in spirits
an erg is a unit of energy

explanation.surface: Feeling low again about energy as the light dims.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow left in the sky after sunset is light that is fading.

clue.text: Be special in final performance?

indicators.note: the special letter goes inside the final performance word

parts.note: an actor's exit is the last thing done on stage, a whimsical final performance

explanation.surface: Be outstanding in your last show.
explanation.definitionFit: To be, in the sense of having being, is to exist.

clue.text: US city is enthralled by source of computer data denying Democrat corruption?

indicators.note: the city and is are held captive inside the next piece
the disc loses the Democrat letter

parts.note: a CD-ROM is a disc holding computer data
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A political story: a US city in thrall to a data source with no Democrat, hinting at sleaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The data source is a CD-ROM disc; 'denying' removes the Democrat letter from it, leaving CROM to hold the city and 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring friends with appointments is a kind of corruption, hence the question mark.

clue.text: My job has little time for old tree

indicators.note: a short time letter stands in for the old letter

parts.note: a role is a job or function
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone's work leaves them no time for an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In ROLE, the O (old) is swapped for T (time), giving RTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub or small tree with fragrant leaves.
